<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin="par112"/>parallel with a simple imperfect); 9:25, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=4}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=4}} f. a series of frequentative perfects consecutive is interrupted by an imperfect consecutive, while a simple imperfect (as the ''modus rei repetitae'') forms the conclusion. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=17}} a similar perfect is expressly marked, by placing the tone on the final syllable (according to {{GHGpar|49|h}}), as parallel with the real perfects consecutive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|ee}}
Rem. The loose connexion of ''tempora frequentativa'' by {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}} (cf. the Rem. on y and bb) is also very common in this sense; thus with a following perfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=41}} f. (but in verse 42''<sup>a</sup>'', where the verb is separated from the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} by an insertion, we find {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יָשִׂים|translate=he used not to put them in}}, according to {{GHGpar|107|e}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ff. (see above, e), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=23}} (followed by five perfects consecutive); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=5}}; with a following imperfect (as the ''modus rei repetitae''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=2|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=26}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=12|verse=5}} f. {{GHGheb|text=והיה}}, contrary to what would be expected, is continued by means of the imperfect consecutive, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=22}} by {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא}} with the perfect (instead of the imperfect).

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|ff}}
'''5.''' Further, the perfect consecutive is very frequently employed with a certain emphasis to introduce the apodosis after sentences (or their equivalents) which contain a condition, a reason, or a statement of time. Such an apodosis, as in the cases already treated, may represent either future events, or commands and wishes, or even events which have been often repeated in the past. Thus—

(''a'') The perfect consecutive occurs in the apodosis to conditional sentences<ref>In a number of the examples of this kind the protasis is already loosely connected by means of {{GHGheb|text=והיה}}, and hence some of them had to be already mentioned above, under y, bb, ee.</ref> ({{GHGpar|159|g}}, o, s):

(α) After {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} with the imperfect, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=4}}b {{GHGheb|text=אִם־יְמִיתֻ֫נוּ וָמָֽתְנוּ|translate=if they kill us}}, (well then) ''we shall but die''; here the perfect consecutive is used obviously with greater emphasis than the imperfect ({{GHGheb|text=נִחְיֶה}}) which immediately precedes; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, 41, 32:9, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=30|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=11}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|gg}}
(β) After {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} with the perfect (in the sense of a ''futurum exactum''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=20}}, 7<sup>4''a''</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=4|verse=4}} f.; as precative apodosis after {{GHGheb|text=אִם־נָא}} with the ''perf. preteritum'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=10}}; as a frequentative perfect consecutive, to represent past events in the apodosis after {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} with a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=4}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} with imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|hh}}
(γ) After {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} (''in case, suppose that'') with the imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=13}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=19}} a question appears to be expressed by the perfect consecutive, ''for if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away?'' Probably, however, with Klostermann, {{GHGheb|text=וּמִי}} should be read for {{GHGheb|text=וְכִי}}.</ref> Frequentative with reference to the past, after {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} with frequentative perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=2|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=13}}f.<section end="par112"/><noinclude>
